content: The primary goal in the treatment of individuals with type 2 diabetes who are overweight or obese should be effective weight management. Clinical evidence indicates that achieving even a modest weight reduction, typically around 3-7% of total body weight, can result in significant improvements in glycemic control. This improvement in blood glucose levels facilitates better overall diabetes management. Furthermore, moderate weight loss has been shown to decrease the dependency on glucose-lowering medications, enhance the body’s sensitivity to insulin, and, in some cases, contribute to the potential for long-term remission of type 2 diabetes.
